cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has been carrying the LORD's message to Jerusalem: wake up, because the LORD has comforted His people and redeemed Jerusalem (Isaiah 52:1, 9). Now the LORD points to someone and calls Him My Servant. The first thing He says is that this Servant will prosper.

cards.question: The LORD says His Servant will prosper. What else does He say will happen to the Servant?

answers.text: He will be lifted up high
He will stay hidden away
He will rule from Babylon

cards.text: Raised. Lifted up. Highly exalted. Friend, that's THREE ways to say UP in one sentence, and then the LORD says something hard: many were appalled at Him.

cards.question: Many were appalled at the Servant. True or false: His form is described as marred beyond human likeness.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then it flips: He will sprinkle many nations, and KINGS will shut their mouths because of Him. Kings, friend, the folks who give speeches for a living, sitting there with NOTHING to say.

cards.question: Why do kings shut their mouths because of the Servant?

answers.text: They see what they were never told
They lose a war against Israel
He orders them to keep quiet

cards.text: Now the voice turns to "we": "Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?" Two questions, back to back.

cards.question: True or false: the question "Who has believed our message?" sounds like everybody already believes it.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then comes a picture of the Servant growing up before Him like a tender shoot, like a root out of dry ground.

cards.question: The Servant grew up like a root out of dry ground. What do the speakers say about how He looked?

answers.text: Nothing in His looks drew people in
He looked like a king in a palace
Crowds came just to see His face

cards.text: Then it gets heavy: "He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief." I spent years forgotten in a junk drawer, friend, and that doesn't even come close.

cards.question: The Servant was despised and rejected. How was He treated?

answers.text: Like someone people hide their faces from
Like someone people run to for help
Like someone people crown as their king

cards.text: Now here's the turn. He took up our infirmities, and He carried our sorrows.

cards.question: The Servant carried their sorrows. But what did the speakers think was happening to Him?

answers.text: That God had struck Him down
That He was hiding from God
That He was faking His pain

cards.text: And then comes the BUT. He was pierced for our transgressions, and He was crushed for our iniquities.

cards.question: The speakers talk about a punishment that brought them peace. Who did that punishment fall on?

answers.text: The Servant
The speakers themselves
The kings who saw Him

cards.question: True or false: the speakers say they are healed by the Servant's stripes.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then the speakers own it: we all, like sheep, have gone astray, and each one has turned to his own way. That's me ignoring my GPS while it begs, "Recalculating… RECALCULATING."

cards.question: The speakers have all gone astray like sheep. The LORD has laid upon the Servant the ___ of us all.

answers.text: iniquity
care
hope

cards.text: Now watch how He takes it all: "He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth." Me? I bump my gold base on the oven door and the whole Dorinverse hears about it.

cards.question: The Servant stays silent while He is oppressed. Which animal is He compared to?

answers.text: A lamb led to the slaughter
A goat sent into the wilderness
A dove caught in a net

cards.text: As a sheep before her shearers is silent, He stays quiet. By oppression and judgment He was taken away, cut off from the land of the living.

cards.question: The Servant is cut off from the land of the living. True or false: He was stricken for His own transgression.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Even His grave says something. He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in His death.

cards.question: The Servant was given a grave with the wicked. What do we learn about how He lived?

answers.text: He did no violence and told no lies
He fought back against His enemies
He hid the truth to stay safe

cards.text: Then comes the hardest line in the whole passage: it was the LORD's will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer. But friend, the passage doesn't stop there.

cards.question: When His soul is made a guilt offering, the Servant will see His ___.

answers.text: offspring
enemies
accusers

cards.text: He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand. After the anguish of His soul, He will see the light of life and be satisfied.

cards.question: The LORD calls Him My righteous Servant. What will the Servant do for many?

answers.text: Justify them and bear their iniquities
Judge them and send them away
Teach them and then leave them

cards.text: So the LORD says He will give the Servant a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong. Strong? Friend, I lose wrestling matches to cold cookie dough.

cards.question: Why does the LORD give the Servant a portion with the great?

answers.text: He poured out His life unto death
He won a war against the kings
He built a house for the LORD

cards.text: He was numbered with the transgressors. Yet He bore the sin of many.

cards.question: The Servant was numbered with the transgressors. True or false: He made intercession for them.

answers.text: True
False
